title: No source publishes the operation that carries a stage outcome and a service level breach from rwb-guarantee to rwb-case
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 3, 5, 13, 19, 41); _work/msr/context/S3.md (ownership rows); Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 (T-A.1, T5.2); legacy RWB-E4-015 Endpoints
section: s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 3, 9 and 10; s9 State transitions; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes
description: The application story reports each GUARANTEE target state to the parent CaseWorkflow and raises one service level breach per lost claim, and neither fact has a published operation. Architecture v5 slide 13 gives S3 a Temporal call to rwb-case and an event subscription and no REST operation of P3; the Ownership Map lists the two S3 claim operations only and no operation of its neighbours; TSD S3 T5.2 says calls go through the published Java interfaces of P3 and names none. The story therefore builds against the workflow boundary (the child-workflow return the parent applies) and a placeholder REST answer, and the breach clock, its task and its escalation are taken as rwb-case's.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 13 matrix: row S3 Guarantee, column P3 Case = T, column P6 Comms = T E, and no R; the Ownership Map API rows for S3 are POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims and PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId} only; TSD S3 T5.2 names the P3, P4, P5, P6 and P7 interfaces without an operation name; the Ownership Map gives S3 zero jobs and zero events.
owner_role: P3 rwb-case owner with the S3 rwb-guarantee owner
proposed: The P3 owner publishes the stage-outcome and breach operation with its shape before the wave 3 tag, and RWB-S3-E4015-CON replaces the placeholder in a minor version with no behaviour change.

title: The stall horizon, the warning window and the breach escalation behind 'raises the service level breach' have no value in any source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-015); Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (A2.3.1, A2.3.3.1); Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 (T4); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-GUA-05, R-GUA-09)
section: s8 BR6; s13 Configuration and reference data; s14 Validation and messages; s19 Out of scope
description: Legacy AC1 asks for the breach 'if it stalls' and AC2 and AC3 ask for the breach to be reported when the claim deadline is missed, but no source read for this key gives the stall horizon, the warning window of the deadline, the escalation path or the wording of the breach task. The FSD fixes the measure (claims filed inside the deadline, 100 percent) and no threshold; the routing workbook gives R-GUA-05 and R-GUA-09 a Timer column of None. The values are therefore versioned rule and reference rows of the business and rwb-case's task data, never constants of this build, and their content stays a placeholder.
evidence: FSD S3 A2.3.1 metric row gives no threshold; FSD S3 A2.3.3.1 lists VR-S3-003-1, R-GUA-05, R-GUA-09 and BR-S3-003 only; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-GUA-05 and R-GUA-09 carry 'None' in the Timer column and name 'Workbench, Workbench scheduler' as systems; TSD S3 T4 names the states and no window.
owner_role: S3 rwb-guarantee owner with the P3 rwb-case owner and the business rule owner
proposed: The business owner fixes the stall horizon, the warning window and the escalation as versioned rule and reference rows before the wave 3 tag; the story reads them and changes in no code.

title: The GUARANTEE rule package and the two claim lists are consumed with no dependency row in this slice
source: _work/msr/context/S3.md (DP table, ownership rows); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (RWB-S3-E4015-APP H, C, I, X); Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 (T3.2, T4)
section: s3 Preconditions; s7 Target reading; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s13 Configuration and reference data
description: The story evaluates the GUARANTEE route set at its version in force and reads LOV-CLAIM-STATUS and LOV-CLAIM-TYPE at their version, and neither the package of rwb-decision (P7) nor the reference data of rwb-case (P3) appears in the dependency rows of the slice. DP-04 and DP-07 are not in the pattern set of this key either, so no H or C row is added. The story reads them on their contracts and on a test fixture, and the absence of the row is recorded here rather than hidden.
evidence: split_plan.json slice RWB-S3-E4015-APP carries H = RWB-S3-E4015-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON and empty C, I, X; the pattern list of the key is DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19; TSD S3 T4 states 32 rules over 17 states held in the Business Rules and Routing Logic workbook; TSD S3 T3.2 names the two lists.
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the P3 rwb-case owner
proposed: The planner adds the two contract rows (P7 package, P3 reference data) at the next plan revision, or the platform declares both as template capabilities; the story then drops the fixture and uses the published answer.

title: No source publishes the payment-fact read of rwb-source-data that replaces the legacy v_ace_payment read
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (A2.3); Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 (T5.1, T5.2); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 29, 37, 41); legacy RWB-E4-015 Data table
section: s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 11; s11 Data; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes
description: The legacy data table reads v_ace_payment (DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054) for the payment code, account key, date, amount, channel and capital amount, and the target forbids a direct read because only rwb-source-data holds a v_ace_* grant. DP-05 in this key's pattern set is exactly that prohibition, and it adds no dependency. The owner's read operation and the shape of its answer are published by no source read here, so the story builds the client against a documented use and a fixture, and no view, no account table and no balance is read or stored here.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-015 Data table row 'v_ace_payment'; Architecture v5 slide 29 notes state that the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views are read only by rwb-source-data; slide 41 gives S3 the guarantee claim only; TSD S3 T5.2 names the cross-module interfaces of P3, P4, P5, P6 and P7 and none of P1.
proposed: The P1 owner publishes the payment-fact read before the wave 3 tag; the client and its fake are replaced by the published answer in a minor version with no behaviour change.

title: No REQ-S3 identifier is given for this legacy key by any source
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 (T8); Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (Requirements served); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md; _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json (RWB-E4-015)
description: TSD S3 T8 maps REQ-S3-001 to REQ-S3-007 to FEAT-GUA-01 and carries no per-story row, the FSD lists the seven requirements against the module and not against the feature, and the Epics 3 to 8 specification carries feature IDs only; the legacy index of the key has an empty requirement list. The story therefore traces to FEAT-GUA-03 and to REQ-S3-002 as the requirement the FSD text supports, and the PRD is expected to add the identifiers.
evidence: TSD S3 T8 rows all read FEAT-GUA-01 with the story column 'Written one epic ahead'; FSD S3 'Requirements served' lists REQ-S3-001 to REQ-S3-007 with epic E4 and no feature; legacy_index.json row RWB-E4-015 has reqs = [].
owner_role: Requirements owner with the S3 rwb-guarantee owner
proposed: The PRD of rwb-guarantee links the key to a REQ-S3 identifier at C1; the traceability rows of both stories are then updated with no other change.

title: The source names the three claim entities and the eight columns, and states no element list, no 409 cause and no field for the lost-claim reason and amount
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 (T-A.1, T-A.2, T3.1, T3.2); Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 (A2.6.3.2, A2.8.3.2 field catalog); legacy RWB-E4-015 Validation and messages
section: s2 Business rationale; s4 Flow steps 3 to 6; s7 AC2, AC5; s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s13 Element surface; s14 Validation and messages
description: TSD S3 T-A.2 names GuaranteeClaimRequest, GuaranteeClaim and GuaranteeClaimUpdate and the two error sets, and T3.1 gives the eight guarantee_claim fields with their physical types; no source enumerates the elements of the two request schemas, states what the 409 of the patch means, or gives a field identifier for the lost-claim reason and the lost amount that R-GUA-05 and R-GUA-09 record. The contract publishes the table's fields in camelCase, a partial update of filedAt, paidAmount and status, a 409 of a claim whose status does not admit the patch, and no element for the reason and the amount; each of those is a working read and none is a value invented in the document. The 404 and 503 message texts are in the same position.
evidence: TSD S3 T-A.2 tables list Purpose, Request, Response, Errors, Authorization and Idempotency and no field list; T3.1 lists DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 only; the FSD field catalog of A2.6.3.2 and A2.8.3.2 repeats the same seven claim fields and no reason or amount column; the legacy message set of RWB-E4-015 holds MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003 only.
owner_role: S3 rwb-guarantee owner with the S3 data owner
proposed: The S3 data owner confirms the element list of the two request schemas, the cause of the 409 and whether the lost-claim reason and amount take a column of guarantee_claim; the DB story adds the column in its own Flyway sequence if it is confirmed, and the contract republishes in a minor version.
